title: Language Membership and Midpoint Chains
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every input string $y$ there is a time $T$ such that every choice string of length $T$ makes $N$ halt, uses at most $sp(|y|)$ work-tape cells, and $y\in L$ exactly when some such choice string makes $N$ halt with output $[\mathrm{true}]$. For any Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $s,w$ satisfying $sp(|x|)\le s$, $\mathrm{codeLen}(N,|x|,s)\le w$, and $\mathrm{configBound}(|x|,s)\le 2^w$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of length-$w$ bit strings $A,B$ such that the initial configuration of $N$ on $x$ is encoded by the first $\mathrm{codeLen}(N,|x|,s)$ bits of $A$, $B$ encodes a halting configuration with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, and $A$ and $B$ are related by $w$ levels of midpoint subdivision using the relation that holds when two strings agree or encode a single machine step within the space window $s$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$L$ is a language of Boolean strings
caveat: The conclusion has been paraphrased via the supplied encoding definitions; midpoint subdivision and the block relations have dataset descriptions pending, so their exact decoding conventions are not available in the payload.
